cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The seating plan is fine. If your parents are at different tables, the place cards were moved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They weren't. You printed Mum at table two and Dad at seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the column headings before calling it a seating plan. Two is her meal choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An old heading. Cross it out; the venue has treated a working sheet as the final plan.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 blames moved place cards; A3 corrects B2's reading as a meal-choice column; A5 reclassifies B4's authored template as an obsolete working sheet to shift responsibility to the venue.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 printed table numbers defeat A1 movement explanation. A3 offers a column explanation; B4 names the heading and author, causing A5 to attack document status instead.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants parents seated correctly and B4 checks the actual heading. These are ordinary checks by someone affected by A's plan.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's proof of A's authorship to escalate from disputed column meaning to a claim that the venue used the wrong document version.

specificity.evidence: A1 seating plan and separated parents, B2 table numbers and B4 labeled template make the practical dispute clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's cross-it-out instruction and draft-status claim are a compact defensive correction. No extra claim-processing joke is appended.
